### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. SERKAL syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.739)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-373080, Reactome:R-HSA-3772470, Reactome:R-HSA-4086400, Reactome:R-HSA-3238698, Reactome:R-HSA-201681)

**Proposed mechanism:** WNT4 (HGNC:12783) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP511); Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP511) —LEADS_TO→ Mullerian duct aplasia (HP:0000001); Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP511) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperandrogenism (HP:0004774); Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP511) —LEADS_TO→ Caudal regression sequence (HP:0001732); Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP511) —LEADS_TO→ Renal agenesis (HP:0000053). Loss-of-function mutations in WNT4 disrupt the Wnt signaling pathway, leading to a spectrum of phenotypes including mullerian duct aplasia and hyperandrogenism in mullerian aplasia and hyperandrogenism, and caudal regression sequence and renal agenesis in SERKAL syndrome. The shared disruption of the Wnt signaling pathway constitutes the mechanistic overlap.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of individuals with mullerian aplasia and hyperandrogenism or SERKAL syndrome who harbor pathogenic variants in genes other than WNT4, or where WNT4 variants are demonstrably not loss-of-function, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs148636760)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of WNT4 in these developmental disorders could lead to targeted therapeutic strategies for improving reproductive health and addressing other developmental anomalies in affected individuals.

Loss-of-function mutations in WNT4 and WNT7A disrupt the planar cell polarity pathway. This disruption leads to the phenotypes observed in mullerian aplasia and hyperandrogenism (Disease A) and phocomelia, Schinzel type (Disease B).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in WNT4 or WNT7A in individuals with mullerian aplasia and hyperandrogenism, and similarly for phocomelia, Schinzel type, would support this hypothesis. Conversely, if individuals with one disease lack variants in these genes, or if variants are found to have gain-of-function effects, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: gnomAD analysis showing common benign variants in WNT4 or WNT7A in the general population that are also present in affected individuals.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of WNT4 and WNT7A in the planar cell polarity pathway could lead to the development of targeted therapies for both mullerian aplasia and hyperandrogenism and phocomelia, Schinzel type, potentially by modulating WNT signaling.
